title: Rust Statements and Expressions knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Rust Statements and Expressions”?
options: Rust Statements and Expressions is one building block of this area: Read Rust syntax and use bindings, scalar types, numeric conversions, and formatting safely. questions.answer_key: Rust Statements and Expressions is one building block of this area: Read Rust syntax and use bindings, scalar types, numeric conversions, and formatting safely. Start with the smallest example, identify the inputs and assumptions, and check the edge cases before using the technique in a larger program.
questions.explanation: Rust Statements and Expressions is one building block of this area: Read Rust syntax and use bindings, scalar types, numeric conversions, and formatting safely. questions.prompt: What is the most dependable way to apply “Rust Statements and Expressions” in a new program?
options: Start with a minimal example, state its assumptions, verify the expected behavior, and test a relevant boundary case.
Change several unrelated implementation details until the output looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and errors if the program appears to work once.
Use nightly-only features by default even when stable Rust is sufficient.
questions.answer_key: Start with a minimal example, state its assumptions, verify the expected behavior, and test a relevant boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproductions and explicit boundary tests make the behavior easier to verify and maintain.

questions.prompt: When a result involving “Rust Statements and Expressions” differs from your prediction, what should you do first?
options: Reduce the case, inspect the inputs and full diagnostic/error, check the supported toolchain or dependency, and retry one change at a time.
Suppress the error without investigating it.
Assume the compiler is wrong and disable checks globally.
Add an unrelated dependency before reproducing the issue.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the case, inspect the inputs and full diagnostic/error, check the supported toolchain or dependency, and retry one change at a time.
questions.explanation: A reproducible failure and precise diagnostic are the best starting points for debugging.
